text:
Priya K: Heads up — seeing a large spike of streaming reconnect loops in prod-west after the routing policy swap. Clients keep retrying and many are getting 401s on resume attempts.
Elliot: Oof. Is this the cheap-region-first routing change that went out ~10:15?
Priya K: Yeah that one. Telemetry shows a burst right after rollout. console -> routes -> sessions shows reconnects/min jumping from ~120 to ~6k.
Sam: Any logs? 401 on resume usually means token/session mismatch.
Priya K: Paste from the proxy logs: 
```
[2026-03-18T10:17:34Z] conn=xyz resume attempt token=rt:abc123 result=401 reason="resume-token-rotated"
[2026-03-18T10:17:34Z] conn=xyz client_retries=8 backoff_ms=1500
[2026-03-18T10:17:35Z] conn=abc resume attempt token=rt:abc123 result=200 -> accepted
[2026-03-18T10:17:35Z] conn=def resume attempt token=rt:old456 result=401 reason="token-not-found"
```
Priya K: Looks like some requests were routed to nodes that had already rotated session keys — others hit nodes still accepting the old resume token. Sticky-routing fallback was failing.
Marta: So the cheap-region policy routed an existing connection to a new pool which didn't share the transient resume-token state.
Elliot: Right — we depended on in-memory resume tokens being present. New pool had different token store.
Sam: Quick mitigation: accept resume tokens for an extra grace window on auth-service and add a short-lived distributed cache for resume tokens. Could we patch prod to accept old tokens for 60s?
Priya K: Can we hotfix that without a full deploy? Maybe a config toggle on auth to relax `strict_resume_check` to false.
Sam: Yes — runbook below.
```
# temporary on-call mitigation
curl -X POST https://auth.prod-west.internal/_admin/flags \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"strict_resume_check": false, "resume_grace_secs": 60}'
```
Sam: I pushed the flag in prod-west, monitoring now.
Marta: Also adding a console dashboard panel to show resume_fail_rate / resume_success_rate by node so we can spot mismatched nodes.
Elliot: Long-term we need resume tokens in a shared cache (redis) or make resume header include node-id that can be routed back. Either that or ensure sticky routing is honored during rollouts.
Priya K: Agreed. For immediate follow-up: (1) revert cheap-region-first rollout for streaming routes; (2) enable the grace window; (3) add redis-backed resume store ticket.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-342 — Streaming resume auth failures in prod-west (priority P2). Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-342
Priya K: Reverted the routing policy at 10:28. reconnect rate dropped to baseline in ~90s. :thumbsup:
Marta: Opening infra ticket to add `resume_cache` to deployment blueprint and a dashboard. Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-infra.
Elliot: Also note: client SDKs should optionally include a `Resume-Node` header to prefer same node where possible — filing DEVSX-912.
Sam: Postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause (resume token not global + routing swap), immediate mitigation (grace window + rollback), permanent fix (shared resume store or durable token replication).
Priya K: Thanks all. If anyone sees a second wave ping here.
Elliot: Adding a small unit test to insure resume token check behavior when routing to a different node. Will PR.
Sam: PR landed for the flag playbook docs.
Priya K: Closing incident after 45m of monitoring with no regressions.
__notes: Thread-length kept realistic: short Slack messages with a few code/log blocks and @-style bot message. No title field included per agents.md.
